h1: The 6 Best Docking Stations for Laptops of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Laptop Docking Stations: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six laptop docking stations, sorted by monitor support, power delivery, Thunderbolt certification and port count.
summary: The UGREEN Revodok Max 208 is the best dock for most people, with certified Thunderbolt 4, 40Gbps and support for dual 4K displays at a mid price. The Plugable TBT-UDM is the driverless, certified alternative, and the Anker Prime 14-port is the pick for sheer port count and power. The UGREEN Revodok Pro and the Anker 8-in-1 are the budget docks for dual monitors.
intro: The most common dock mistake is buying a USB-C hub and expecting it to behave like a Thunderbolt dock. The two look alike, but they differ in how many monitors they can drive, how fast they move data and how much power they push back into your laptop, and the box rarely makes that obvious.

Our read of six docks comes from spec sheets and what owners report after long desk use. We ranked them on monitor support, power delivery, data speed, port variety and value. Two thinner listings were left out because their specs did not give enough detail to recommend.

products.name: UGREEN 8-in-1 Thunderbolt 4 Docking Station (Revodok Max 208)
products.verdict: Certified Thunderbolt 4 with 40Gbps at a better price than the competition.
products.description:
The Revodok Max 208 is a certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with 40Gbps bandwidth and three Thunderbolt 4 ports. It drives dual 4K at 60Hz or a single 8K display, provides 85W charging, and adds Gigabit Ethernet and three USB-A 3.2 ports.

It takes first place because it brings certified Thunderbolt to a price below the Plugable. The 85W charging is slightly lower than the 100W of its rival, so large laptops may charge slowly under load.

Buy it if you use a Mac with an M1 through M4 Pro or Max chip, or any Thunderbolt laptop, and want guaranteed compatibility.

products.name: Plugable Thunderbolt 4 Dock (TBT-UDM)
products.verdict: A certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with 100W charging and no drivers to install.
products.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is certified Thunderbolt 4, charges at 100W and sets up without drivers. It supports dual 4K over HDMI or a single 6K display, with six USB ports, an SD card slot and Ethernet.

It ranks just behind the UGREEN because it tops out at a 6K single display and costs more for the same certification. The 100W charging and driverless setup are the reasons to pick it, particularly on larger laptops.

Choose it if you want guaranteed Thunderbolt compatibility and easy setup rather than a hub that merely should work.

products.name: Anker Prime Docking Station 14-Port
products.verdict: The dock with the most ports and the highest total power output.
products.description:
The Anker Prime 14-port dock offers up to 160W of total output, 10Gbps data transfer and dual 4K display support. It works with Dell, HP, Lenovo and other Windows laptops.

It ranks third because it is built around USB-C at 10Gbps, not Thunderbolt at 40Gbps, so it cannot match the speed of the first two. The payoff is the 14 ports and the large power budget, which can charge a laptop and other devices at once.

Buy it for a crowded desk with many accessories. Skip it if you need certified Thunderbolt.

products.name: Anker Nano 13-in-1 Laptop Docking Station
products.verdict: A dock for the desk plus a travel hub you can unplug.
products.description:
The Anker Nano 13-in-1 has a detachable 6-in-1 hub and supports three displays at once, using two HDMI ports and one DisplayPort. It adds 10Gbps USB-C, three USB-A ports and up to 100W Power Delivery.

It ranks fourth because it is a USB-C dock at 10Gbps, so it is slower than the Thunderbolt picks, and it costs similar money. The three display support and the removable hub are the standout features.

Choose it if you want a triple monitor setup and a hub you can carry on trips.
products.idealFor: Triple monitor desks that also travel.

products.name: UGREEN 7-in-1 Docking Station (Revodok Pro)
products.verdict: Dual 4K at 60Hz and fast data ports for under $50.
products.description:
The Revodok Pro is a 7-in-1 USB-C dock with two 4K at 60Hz HDMI outputs, 10Gbps USB-A and USB-C data ports and 100W Power Delivery passthrough. It has an aluminum body.

It ranks fifth because the port count is limited and there is no Ethernet listed. For the price it delivers dual 4K at 60Hz that many pricier hubs struggle with.

It suits budget buyers who want two sharp monitors and fast data without extras.

products.name: Anker Laptop Docking Station 8-in-1
products.verdict: Dual HDMI, Ethernet and 85W passthrough at a low price.
products.description:
This Anker 8-in-1 hub has two HDMI ports for dual 4K monitor support, Gigabit Ethernet, 85W Power Delivery passthrough and an SD card slot.

It ranks last because it is the oldest design here and the least future proof, though it covers the basics at a low price in the $50 to $100 range. It lacks the faster data ports of the UGREEN Revodok Pro.

Choose it for a home office that needs dual monitors and wired internet without much spending.
products.idealFor: Home offices on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want the fastest data ports.

whatMatters.detail: Thunderbolt 4 is a certified standard with 40Gbps and guaranteed display support, while USB-C docks vary in speed and features. Certified docks remove guesswork about compatibility. Look for the words Thunderbolt 4 certified, and check that your laptop has a Thunderbolt port.

A dock lists how many displays it can run and at what resolution and refresh. Dual 4K at 60Hz is common, while some docks drop to 30Hz. Check the exact refresh rate and whether the numbers apply to your laptop's graphics.

The dock sends power back to the laptop through the cable. A dock that delivers less than your charger can leave a laptop draining under load. Compare the dock's wattage to your laptop's charger and aim for equal or higher.
10Gbps USB ports move files far faster than older 5Gbps ones. This matters for external SSDs. Look for the Gbps figure beside each port in the listing.
Wired Ethernet gives a steadier connection than Wi Fi for video calls. SD readers help photographers. Decide which extras you will use daily and check each is listed.

faq.q: Will a dock work with my laptop?
faq.a: It depends on your laptop's port. A USB-C dock needs video output support, and a Thunderbolt dock needs a Thunderbolt port. Check your laptop's spec page.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a dock?
faq.a: Assuming all USB-C ports are equal. Some laptops cannot output video or charge through USB-C.

faq.q: Is Thunderbolt worth it over a USB-C hub?
faq.a: If you run multiple displays and fast storage, yes. For one monitor and basic use, a cheaper USB-C dock is fine.

faq.q: How do I set up two monitors?
faq.a: Connect the dock to your laptop, plug each monitor into a separate HDMI or DisplayPort, then arrange them in your display settings.

faq.q: How do I keep a dock cool?
faq.a: Leave room around the dock, especially aluminum ones that act as a heat sink, and avoid stacking items on top.

faq.q: Can one dock charge my laptop at full speed?
faq.a: Only if its power delivery matches your laptop's charger. An 85W dock may charge a 100W laptop slowly under load.

finalTake: The UGREEN Revodok Max 208 is the dock to buy for most Thunderbolt and Mac users. The Plugable TBT-UDM is the easy driverless option, and the Anker Prime 14-port suits crowded desks. For dual monitors on a budget, take the UGREEN Revodok Pro.
